rearm_rc.credit: debounce and one-edge formation only; never the sole anti-auto-start barrier

firmware_contract.reset_outputs: PA25 and PA23 default low through external 10-kohm pulldowns: hazardous permit is held off while S3 reset remains released
firmware_contract.boot_rule: never release PA25 after self-test while RUN_EDGE is high; require 500 ms continuously low first
firmware_contract.fault_rule: assert PA25 low immediately, store the cause, and require a new qualified KILL-to-RUN cycle
firmware_contract.s3_recovery: PA23 may pulse high to reset only S3; release it low after reset so the fault-only UI can reboot

corrections.finding: The prior current-R2 map tied the S3 reset sink to the generic C5 kill gate, so a hard fault could remove the display that must explain the cause.
corrections.correction: M1 contact 36 now carries a separate S3_RESET_KILL_GATE from Safety PA23; C5 and RF RP retain direct fault reset.
corrections.cost_effect: no added fitted body or cost; one former M1 reserve is used

corrections.finding: Safety PA23 had no external reset-state bias and could float during controller reset.
corrections.correction: The unused evidence-mask P17 pulldown is reassigned as a 10-kohm PA23 pulldown; P17 is tied directly to ground.

corrections.finding: Earlier wording credited RC delay alone with blocking auto-start, which is not a sufficient invariant for arbitrary firmware release timing.
corrections.correction: The verified rule holds PA25 low until a continuous physical KILL qualification; RC provides a clean subsequent edge only.

physical_residuals: H8 measures real switch bounce and break-before-make interval.
H8 measures the populated 100-kohm/2.2-uF RC under DC bias and temperature; startup safety does not depend solely on this number.
H8 captures POR assertion/release, direct C5/RF-RP reset and S3 fault-display retention at real rail corners.
